To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) somatoliberins stimulate secretion of growth hormone in primary cultures of adenoma cells from acromegaly patients; 2) somatostatin at low concentrations inhibits secretion of both growth hormone and prolactin in adenoma cells, while at high concentrations it inhibits secretion of prolactins only.
somatoliberins stimulate growth hormone production, while somatostatin suppresses growth hormone secretion in adenoma cells.
somatoliberine stimulates secretion of growth hormones and has no effect upon secretion of prolactine in primary cultures of adenoma cells obtained form acromegalic people.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of somatostin and somatoliberins on the secretion of growth hormone in primary cell cultures of human hypophyseal tumours.
the study of the secretory activity of cultured growth hormone-producing adenomas to somatolibern and somatostation, which are the most important regulatory factors of growth hormone secretion.

the study of the secretory reactions of the adenoma cells of acromegalic hypophysis to somatolibrin and somatotropin, which is a model system for studying the secretory reactions to somatolibern and somatostain of normal hypophyseal cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

somatoliberins stimulate growth hormone and inhibit prolactin production in hypophyseal tumour cells and that somatostatin stimulates growth hormone production in the short-term and inhibits it in the long-term.

somatoliberins are the only hormones that stimulate secretion of growth hormone in the cells of the adenomas of acromegalic origin, and that somatostatin, in a long-term culture, inhibits secretion of prolactine.
somatostatin is a potent inhibitor of the secretion of growth hormone in adenomatous cells and that this inhibitory action of somatostain is abolished or reversed by somatoliberine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the adenoma cells, somatoliberins stimulate growth hormone secretion and inhibit prolactin secretion; somatostatin at high concentrations inhibits both hormones, while at low concentrations, it stimulates growth hormone secretion and inhibits prolactins.
somatostatin has a biphasic effect on the growth hormone production: it inhibits the production at low concentrations, while it stimulates the production at high concentrations.

somatoliberins are the main stimulators of growth hormone secretion in the adenoma cells, and that somatostatin acts only in a long-term manner and is a potent inhibitor of the growth hormone secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
growth hormone secretion from adenoma cells is controlled by somatoliberins and somatostatins, while prolactin secretion from these cells is controlled mainly by somatoliberns.
growth hormone and prolactin are secreted by two separate cell populations in the adenoma, which are differently regulated.
somatostatin and somatoliberins have a different effect on the secretion of prolactine and growth hormone in the adenomas.
